chunks: And by his chain of narration, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Paradise is eager for you, for 'Ammar, Salman, Abu Dharr, and Al-Miqdad.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four companions for whom Paradise is eager according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Transmitted by Al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith utilizes the concept of *al-shawq* (longing) to personify Paradise's desire for these four prominent companions, emphasizing their unique spiritual proximity to the Prophet. In Shia scholarship, this narration is often cited to validate the elevated status of the *Sahaba* who remained steadfast in their allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt, linking their earthly piety directly to eternal reward.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-307 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) God’s Prophet (S) said, “
(O Ali!) Paradise is eager to see you, Ammar, Salman, Abu Tharr and al-Miqdad.”
